# jsonschema

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/codec/jsonschema"
```

Package jsonschema validates JSON documents somebody else wrote against a JSON Schema 2020-12 they publish — a webhook's payload, an OpenAPI request body, another program's configuration — with the standard library alone.

```
v, err := jsonschema.NewValidator(schema, jsonschema.Config{})
report, err := v.Validate(body, 1<<20)
if !report.OK() { … report.Paths() … }
```

The core, applicator and validation vocabularies are compiled; "$ref" resolves within the schema and to the resources Config registers, never over the network; "format" is asserted only for the formats Config.AssertFormats names. Drafts before 2020-12, the dynamic scope, "$vocabulary", the unevaluated and content vocabularies are refused by name. A report's paths follow the validation package's grammar and no message quotes the document.

## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/codec/jsonschema/gen_facade.go>)

Config configures NewValidator — the resources a "$ref" may name, the formats asserted.

```go
type Config = svcjsonschema.Config
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/codec/jsonschema.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config struct {
	// Resources are schema documents a "$ref" may name, by URI: each is a
	// resource at that URI, and at its "$id" when it has one. A reference to
	// any other URI is refused; nothing is fetched.
	Resources     map[string][]byte
	// AssertFormats are the formats asserted rather than annotated:
	// "date-time" (RFC 3339), "uuid" and "email" (an addr-spec). Naming
	// another is refused.
	AssertFormats []string
}
```

<a name="Validator.Validate"></a>
### func \(Validator\) [Validate](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/codec/jsonschema/jsonschema.go>)

```go
func (*Validator) Validate(doc []byte, maxBytes int64) (validation.ReportValue, error)
```

Validate reads doc through strictjson's bounds — at most maxBytes, one value, no duplicated member name — and returns the violations of the schema, located in the validation package's path grammar ("items\[2].name"). A message never quotes the document. An empty report means doc is valid; an error means doc was not read: strictjson's refusal, or ReferenceLoop for a "$ref" cycle that consumes nothing.
